text:
Alex: Heads up — this morning we started seeing intermittent streaming token stalls on us-west gpupool-3, looks like bursts of 50-200ms jitter and some RPC deadline hits. :eyes:
Maria: saw that too, dashboard shows reordering spikes on the east-west fabric around the same time windows. high p99 latency on grpc stream open/append.
Sam: any recent infra changes? kernel, firmware, or route churn?
Alex: no config deploys to the pool. noticed a flurry of BGP flap alerts from the top-of-rack switches 02:03–02:12 UTC.
Tia: linking a short sample trace:
```
stream_id=0x7f2 rpc_deadline=150ms status=DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
tokens_emitted=312 last_ok=02:03:10.345 stall_duration=180ms
net: rx_seq=12345 rx_reorder=14 rx_loss=0
```
Sam: rx_reorder=14 is suspicious. Looks like packet reordering rather than drops. That matches flow-level reordering causing out-of-order ACKs and serialization delay in our streaming layer.
Maria: on Mellanox NICs we saw similar issues when ECMP path hashes flip across ToR pairs during microbursts. Could be a multi-path pinning problem — traffic alternating between fabric paths.
Alex: also saw higher RDMA handshake retries on some hosts (mlx5 driver counters went up). RDMA retransmit can blow out tail latency for small streaming RPCs.
Tia: ops-oncall ran `ethtool -S` on a node, counters showed increased rx_no_buf and rx_missed on one interface. Suspect backplane congestion + path pinning.
oncall-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-134 — "us-west stream jitter / packet reordering" assigned to eng-sre.
Sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) apply per-node policy to prefer single path (disable ECMP for those subnets) 2) disable GSO/LRO/GRO on affected NICs to reduce coalescing reordering 3) pin flows using source-based routing for the gpupool overlay.
Maria: agree. also check HCA firmware and mlx5 driver (we recently rolled 5.15.0->5.17.2 to some nodes). If driver bug, rolling back could help.
Alex: I'm going to push a conservative canary: disable GRO/GSO on 2 hosts and observe p99 for streaming tokens.
Tia: command I used on the canary: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` — did reduce reorders in kernel counters in my quick test.
Sam: if that helps we can push a broader kernel parameter change via kexec or sysctl? note: disabling offloads increases CPU; track token throughput CPU impact.
Maria: another short-term: adjust client-side RPC deadlines (from 150ms -> 300ms) to avoid immediate user-visible errors while we root-cause. Won't fix cost but reduces alarms.
Alex: can we also try per-flow pinning with traffic class? `tc filter` to mark flows and route via single next-hop. Lower blast radius than changing ECMP globally.
Tia: I'll prototype `tc` rule set and test on staging gpupool-2.
Sam: ops note: if RDMA retransmits are the main amplifier, set `rdma_cm` debug and collect `ib_dev` counters; we should capture firmware timestamps and raise with vendor if counts continue.
Maria: created a short checklist in the incident: 1) canary offloads off 2 hosts (Alex) 2) tc pinning PoC (Tia) 3) collect mlx5 & ib counters (Sam) 4) increase client deadlines (Alex) 5) monitor CPU/token throughput (eng-runtime)
Alex: canary applied at 02:28 UTC on gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-18. early telemetry: p99 streaming latency dropped from 230ms->110ms on those nodes and rx_reorder counters dropped to ~1.
Tia: good signal. rolling a 10-host batch with the same ethtool change and tc pinning, will report after 10m. :thumbsup:
Sam: long-term we should consider route-stability fixes: pinning ECMP using 5-tuple hashing at ToR, or enable consistent-hash on fabric to avoid micro-flaps affecting live flows. Also file with vendor re: mlx5 driver that interacts poorly with our ToR switch features.
Maria: +1 on vendor ticket. Also add a test to our canary suite that generates controlled microbursts to catch this earlier.
Alex: moving client deadlines back down after 1h once rollouts prove stable. For now keeping 300ms.
Tia: rolling 10-host change complete at 02:45 UTC — clusterwide p99 dropped ~70ms, RPC deadline alarms reduced by 85%.
Sam: next steps: follow up with network team to check ToR firmware and ECMP churn logs; schedule vendor support if counters reappear.
Alex: thanks all — keeping incident open until next-day. I'll paste final mitigation commands and perf delta in the doc.
Maria: saved canary dashboards and added alert suppression for the escalation window.
Tia: saved `tc` rules snippet to infra-runbooks/gpu-networking (will add link here after CI merge).
Alex: final note for postmortem: cost impact estimate from disabling offloads ~+5% CPU on those nodes for the duration; tradeoff acceptable to keep streams stable.
oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026-134 status: monitoring.
